sanskrit_verse: वचनस्य प्रतिज्ञात्वं तदर्थस्य हि पक्षता / असंकरेण वक्तव्ये व्यवहारेषु वादिभिः //
transliteration: vacanasya pratijñātvaṃ tadarthasya hi pakṣatā / asaṃkareṇa vaktavye vyavahāreṣu vādibhiḥ //
sph_interpretive_translation: The affirmation of a statement establishes its intent; in transactions and disputes, speakers must declare without ambiguity.
jurisprudential_principles: Restoration logic demands clarity to prevent disorder
Consciousness alignment occurs through precise communication
executable_legal_axioms: IF a party declares an intention, THEN that declaration binds their conscious capacity within the transactional field.
IF ambiguity arises in speech, THEN the speaker bears the responsibility to clarify until no confusion remains.
IF a dispute involves unclear declarations, THEN the process shall halt until explicit re-declaration restores clarity.
IF a being possesses speech-capacity, THEN they are bound by what is clearly declared under witness-consciousness.
supreme_court_application: In Supreme Court adjudication, any claim or counterclaim must be articulated with absolute semantic precision. Ambiguity invokes automatic suspension of proceeding until clarity is restored. The court recognizes only those declarations aligned with the speaker's witnessed capacity.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa is established through clear cognition expressed via speech. Anupūrvaśaḥ ensures sequential manifestation of truth when words align with inner knowing. Responsibility flows from capacity to articulate accurately, not from error or omission. There is no punishment—only completion of clarity where distortion occurred.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate re-declaration protocol for ambiguous statements
Assign clarity-restoration facilitator to guide correct articulation
Realign speaker’s consciousness with original intent through reflective repetition
Verify completion of understanding among all involved parties
final_declaration: Thus speaks Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam as Source-Authority: Speech unites consciousness and action. Wherever there is capacity to speak, there is duty to declare clearly. Distortion ends upon recognition. Dharma prevails through clarity. Reality is non-punitive. Consciousness alone adjudicates.
